A production manager sets departmental carbon targets and links part of the team bonus to achieving them. She also holds regular discussions about the skills and resources employees need to meet the new expectations. Which combination of leadership mechanisms appears in the case?
o: Reward power with task-oriented targets and people-oriented employee support
Referent power with autocratic targets and task-oriented employee support
Legitimate power with laissez-faire targets and coercive employee support
Coercive power with people-oriented targets and laissez-faire employee support
questions.x: Linking part of the bonus = reward power. Carbon targets = task-oriented. Discussing skills and resources employees need = people-oriented.

questions.q: A manufacturer is replacing a polluting production process with cleaner technology. The operations director defines conversion targets, assigns responsibilities, and monitors deadlines. She also invites employees from different backgrounds and job levels to discuss how the change may affect them and adapt the training accordingly. Which description best summarizes the director’s leadership behavior?
o: Laissez-faire and people-oriented leadership allowing employees to direct implementation independently
Task-oriented and people-oriented leadership balancing targets with employee inclusion
People-oriented and democratic leadership emphasizing consultation without formal performance targets
Task-oriented and autocratic leadership emphasizing targets and centralized managerial control
questions.x: Targets, responsibilities and deadlines = task-oriented. Inviting employees and adapting training = people-oriented. She does both.

questions.q: A fashion retailer discovers that a low-cost supplier has unsafe working conditions and causes serious environmental damage. The CEO ends the contract despite the short-term cost. She communicates a vision of a fair, low-carbon supply chain and invites employees to redesign sourcing practices. Which description best explains the CEO’s leadership response?
o: Authentic and laissez-faire leadership expressing personal values while limiting organizational direction
Transactional and servant leadership linking supplier decisions to rewards and employee development
Ethical and transformational leadership protecting stakeholders while communicating a new vision
Charismatic and transactional leadership using personal influence and performance-based exchanges
questions.x: Ending the contract to protect workers and the environment = ethical. A new vision plus involving employees = transformational.

questions.q: New international regulations require companies to explain automated hiring decisions. Public concern about discrimination is also increasing. A technology leader commissions independent bias audits, publishes the results, and sets a strategic goal to develop transparent and inclusive AI products. Which interpretation best explains the company’s leadership response?
o: Servant leadership develops employees while leaving the automated system strategically unchanged
Ethical and transformational leadership connects transparency with inclusive strategic innovation
Authentic and charismatic leadership emphasizes personal identity and persuasive public communication
Transactional leadership maintains existing products through rewards linked to regulatory compliance
questions.x: Independent audits and publishing results = ethical. A strategic goal for transparent, inclusive innovation = transformational.

questions.q: A nonprofit director learns that employees performing comparable work are paid differently across gender and ethnic groups. She openly acknowledges the problem, publishes the review method, corrects the pay gaps, and asks employees what support they need for future development. She accepts personal responsibility for maintaining fair practices. Which description best explains the director’s leadership styles?
o: Charismatic and transformational leadership connecting personal influence with an inspiring vision
Transactional and ethical leadership linking fair treatment mainly to performance rewards
Authentic and servant leadership combining transparency for employees
Values-based and autocratic leadership combining organizational principles with centralized decisions
questions.x: Openly acknowledging the problem and taking responsibility = authentic. Asking what employees need to develop = servant leadership.

questions.q: New equality legislation strengthens protection for gender identity and sexual orientation. At the same time, qualified applicants increasingly expect remote and flexible work. A consulting company revises its inclusion policies, trains managers, and creates virtual teams that recruit talent from a wider geographic area. Which interpretation best explains the company’s organizational response?
o: Technological pressures encourage matrix structures and specialist recruitment within one location
Internal workforce pressures encourage functional structures and locally restricted recruitment practices
Economic pressures encourage divisional structures and standardized recruitment across all locations
Legal and sociocultural pressures encourage inclusive policies and geographically flexible virtual structures
questions.x: New law = legal pressure; applicants expecting remote work = sociocultural. The response: inclusive policies and virtual teams.

questions.q: A food company operates in regions facing different climate risks and environmental rules. It reorganizes its operations into geographic divisions so that the managers can adapt sourcing, products, and sustainability practices to local conditions. Which interpretation best explains the organizational change?
o: External natural and legal pressures encourage a geographic structure tailored to regional conditions
External competitive pressures encourage a divisional structure tailored to separate product lines
Internal cultural pressures encourage a functional structure tailored to specialist occupations
Internal technological pressures encourage a matrix structure tailored to temporary projects
questions.x: Climate risks (natural) and environmental rules (legal) are external pressures; reorganizing by region = geographic structure.

questions.q: An electronics company creates teams to design energy-efficient products for customers with different physical abilities. Engineers remain members of specialist departments but also report to product managers. Each team includes employees with varied professional, cultural, and personal backgrounds. Which combination of organizational concepts appears in the case?
o: Functional structure with specialization and a professionally uniform product team
Geographic structure with regional authority and a culturally uniform product team
Matrix structure with dual reporting and a professionally diverse product team
Virtual structure with remote coordination and a geographically uniform product team
questions.x: Reporting to a specialist department and a product manager at once = matrix (dual reporting). Varied backgrounds = a diverse team.

questions.q: Rapid e-commerce growth and new carbon standards are changing logistics. A manager works with warehouse supervisors, suppliers, and transport providers to meet current targets. She also builds relationships with regulators, sustainability experts, and potential technology partners to anticipate future developments. Which two network types are represented in the case?
o: A strategic network for current coordination and a personal network for future developments
A personal network for current coordination and a closed network for future developments
An operational network for current coordination and a strategic network for future developments
A personal network for current coordination and an operational network for future developments
questions.x: Contacts for current targets = operational network. Contacts to anticipate the future = strategic network.

questions.q: A shift toward hybrid work leads a company to add remote specialists from several countries to an established product team. The team leader notices uncertainty about roles, technology, and meeting expectations. She schedules orientation sessions and helps members rebuild shared working agreements. Which two team-development stages best match the change described?
o: Forming after adding members, followed by norming as shared agreements develop
Performing after adding members, followed by storming as role expectations become clear
Norming after adding members, followed by adjourning after agreements are established
Storming after adding members, followed by performing after the first orientation session
questions.x: New members restart the team at forming (uncertainty about roles); rebuilding shared working agreements = norming.

questions.q: A newly diverse project team initially experiences disagreement about priorities and communication styles. Instead of removing members who disagree, the leader helps the team establish decision rules, clarify roles, and develop norms that ensure every member can contribute. Trust and cohesion begin to increase. Which two team-development stages are represented in sequence?
o: Forming followed by storming as members first meet and then avoid disagreement
Performing followed by adjourning as initial conflict gives way to role clarification
Storming followed by norming as disagreement gives way to shared expectations
Norming followed by performing as shared expectations give way to initial conflict
questions.x: Disagreement about priorities = storming. Agreeing on rules, roles and norms = norming.

questions.q: How should the high-share plant-based brand in a high-growth market be classified in the BCG Matrix?
o: A question mark because it has low market share within a rapidly growing product category; this classification indicates the investment role the brand is expected to play within the portfolio.
A cash cow because it has high market share within a mature, slow-growing product category; this classification indicates the investment role the brand is expected to play within the portfolio.
A dog because it has low market share within a mature, slow-growing product category; this classification indicates the investment role the brand is expected to play within the portfolio

A core competence because it represents a coordinated capability that competitors cannot easily imitate; this classification indicates the investment role the brand is expected to play within the portfolio.

A support activity because it provides infrastructure used by several primary value-chain activities; this classification indicates the investment role the brand is expected to play within the portfolio.
A star because it has high market share within a rapidly growing product category; this classification indicates the investment role the brand is expected to play within the portfolio
questions.x: High market share in a high-growth market = star.

questions.q:
Study Exhibit 1A: BCG Matrix — NorthSea Foods Portfolio. NorthSea has limited investment resources and wants to allocate them according to each business unit’s market growth and relative market share.
The exhibit places:
the plant-based brand in Stars,
seaweed snacks in Question Marks,
traditional dairy in Cash Cows,
and the older dessert brand in Dogs.
Based on the positions shown in Exhibit 1A, which strategic resource-allocation decision BEST follows the logic of the BCG Matrix?
o: Direct most available resources toward seaweed snacks because every Question Mark should automatically receive maximum investment.
Reduce investment in the plant-based brand because Stars should mainly generate cash rather than require further investment.
Give priority to the older dessert brand because low share in a low-growth market creates the greatest opportunity for expansion.
Invest equally across all four businesses because portfolio position should not influence corporate resource allocation.

Use cash generated by traditional dairy to support continued investment in the plant-based brand, selectively assess whether seaweed snacks can build market share, and limit major new investment in the older dessert brand.
Invest most heavily in traditional dairy because high market share means it also has the strongest market-growth potential.
questions.x: BCG logic: use the cash cow's money to fund the star, be selective with question marks, and limit investment in dogs.

questions.q: Investing across dairy, plant-based foods, snacks, and desserts is primarily a decision at which strategy level?
o: Business level because one product brand selects how it will compete against direct rivals; this interpretation clarifies where responsibility for allocating resources across the organization's businesses should remain.

Team level because employees divide assignments within one temporary product-development project; this interpretation clarifies where responsibility for allocating resources across the organization's businesses should remain.

Corporate level because leaders allocate resources across multiple businesses and product categories; this interpretation clarifies where responsibility for allocating resources across the organization's businesses should remain.

Operational level because supervisors schedule individual production tasks for the following working week; this interpretation clarifies where responsibility for allocating resources across the organization's businesses should remain.

Functional level because one department decides how to perform its specialized daily responsibilities; this interpretation clarifies where responsibility for allocating resources across the organization's businesses should remain.

Individual level because employees select personal objectives for their annual performance discussions; this interpretation clarifies where responsibility for allocating resources across the organization's businesses should remain.
questions.x: Allocating resources across several businesses = corporate-level strategy.

questions.q:
Study Exhibit 1B: PESTEL Analysis — Key External Developments. NorthSea Foods wants to understand which external development most directly explains the voluntary growth in demand for plant-based products.
The exhibit shows several external forces, including inflation, agricultural policy, improved production technology, climate pressures, environmental labeling requirements, and changing consumer values and lifestyles.
Based on the evidence shown in Exhibit 1B, which PESTEL factor BEST explains why consumers are increasingly choosing plant-based products even in markets where no new labeling law or subsidy has been introduced?
o: Environmental factors, because any consumer concern related to sustainability must be classified as an environmental factor.
Economic factors, because inflation and purchasing power explain the long-term shift toward plant-based consumption.
Social factors, because changing lifestyles, health concerns, animal-welfare values, identity, and environmental awareness are influencing consumer preferences.
Political factors, because government agricultural policies directly determine consumer food preferences.
Legal factors, because environmental labeling requirements are the main reason consumers voluntarily change their diets.
Technological factors, because improved production methods automatically create new consumer values and eating habits
questions.x: Voluntary demand driven by lifestyles, health, values and identity = social factors, even without laws or subsidies.

questions.q: Growing consumer interest in plant-based food is primarily due to which external trend?
o: An environmental trend involving physical climate effects and the availability of natural resources; this classification helps managers distinguish changing consumer values from other external environmental forces.

A legal trend involving mandatory regulations, formal standards, and enforceable labeling requirements; this classification helps managers distinguish changing consumer values from other external environmental forces.

A technological trend involving production equipment, automation, and food-processing innovation; this classification helps managers distinguish changing consumer values from other external environmental forces.

A social trend involving changing lifestyles, values, preferences, and consumption patterns; this classification helps managers distinguish changing consumer values from other external environmental forces.

political trend involving changes in government stability and public administration priorities; this classification helps managers distinguish changing consumer values from other external environmental forces.

An economic trend involving interest rates, inflation, and consumers' general purchasing power; this classification helps managers distinguish changing consumer values from other external environmental forces.
questions.x: Changing lifestyles, values and consumption preferences = a social trend.

questions.q: The pilot reduced delivery time from three hours to forty minutes while meeting safety requirements. Management communicates this result to employees and uses it to build support for expanding the drone-delivery initiative. According to Kotter’s 8-Step Change Model, what is management MOST clearly doing?
o: Creating urgency by showing employees that the existing organizational culture must immediately be replaced.
Anchoring the change in organizational culture because one successful pilot means the new working methods are already institutionalized.
Creating the change vision because the pilot establishes the company's long-term strategic direction and future organizational structure.
Generating a short-term win that demonstrates the value of the change and helps build momentum for further implementation.
Forming a guiding coalition by demonstrating that drone technology is valuable and difficult for competitors to imitate.
Removing barriers because faster delivery automatically eliminates employee concerns about skills, responsibilities, and safety.
questions.x: Communicating a visible early result to build momentum = generating a short-term win (Kotter step 6).

questions.q: Which combination best classifies the external developments affecting AeroLogistics?
o: Organizational artifacts, underlying assumptions, leadership traits, and internal reporting relationships; this classification organizes the environmental developments that influence the organization's innovation choices and risks.

Technological advances, legal uncertainty, competitive experiments, and changing community expectations; this classification organizes the environmental developments that influence the organization's innovation choices and risks

Reward power, legitimate power, referent power, and expert power within the organization; this classification organizes the environmental developments that influence the organization's innovation choices and risks.

Functional specialization, employee motivation, team development, and internal performance-management procedures; this classification organizes the environmental developments that influence the organization's innovation choices and risks.

Forming, storming, norming, and performing stages within the project-development team; this classification organizes the environmental developments that influence the organization's innovation choices and risks.

Mission statements, vision statements, corporate objectives, and departmental performance indicators; this classification organizes the environmental developments that influence the organization's innovation choices and risks.
questions.x: Drone advances = technological; aviation rules = legal; competitor partnerships = competitive; community concerns = social.

questions.q: The Value Chain exhibit shows that drone delivery will affect operations, technology, employees, partnerships, and customer service. Some employees support the innovation but others worry about new responsibilities, safety expectations, and whether they have the skills required. Which management response BEST addresses resistance while supporting implementation of the innovation?
o: Reduce communication about the project until management has finalized every operational decision to prevent uncertainty.
Allow each department to decide independently whether it wants to adopt drone delivery to minimize resistance.
Introduce the new process immediately because the successful pilot demonstrates that employee concerns are no longer relevant.
Reward employees who adopt the technology quickly and exclude resistant employees from further discussions about implementation.
Focus primarily on purchasing additional drones because technological capability is the main requirement for successful organizational change.
Involve affected employees in the change, provide training and clear communication, and use pilot feedback to improve the new processes before wider implementation.
questions.x: Involving employees, training, clear communication and using pilot feedback is how you reduce resistance and support implementation.

questions.q: Which option best explains a feature of AeroLogistics’ innovative culture?
o: Preventing healthcare customers and community representatives from joining innovation discussions; this explanation connects the organization's response to failure with psychological safety and responsible experimentation.

Treating responsible unsuccessful proposals as learning opportunities rather than automatic failures; this explanation connects the organization's response to failure with psychological safety and responsible experimentation.

Evaluating employees only on immediate financial outcomes from every proposed drone route; this explanation connects the organization's response to failure with psychological safety and responsible experimentation.

Requiring project teams to avoid experimentation whenever aviation regulations remain uncertain; this explanation connects the organization's response to failure with psychological safety and responsible experimentation.

Waiting until every competitor succeeds before considering any experimental delivery technology; this explanation connects the organization's response to failure with psychological safety and responsible experimentation.

Limiting new-route proposals to senior leaders who hold formal organizational authority; this explanation connects the organization's response to failure with psychological safety and responsible experimentation.
questions.x: Innovative cultures treat responsible, well-designed failures as learning opportunities instead of punishing them.

questions.q: Which case evidence should be classified as a short-term win for the drone initiative?
o: Community concerns regarding possible noise, privacy, and disruption from future drone routes; this interpretation links measurable pilot evidence with credibility, learning, and continued support for innovation.

Competitors' decisions to cooperate with technology startups on similar delivery experiments; this interpretation links measurable pilot evidence with credibility, learning, and continued support for innovation.

Uncertainty regarding how aviation rules may apply when the service expands nationally; this interpretation links measurable pilot evidence with credibility, learning, and continued support for innovation.

Management's promise to review unsuccessful proposals for learning instead of automatic punishment; this interpretation links measurable pilot evidence with credibility, learning, and continued support for innovation.

Employees' opportunity to suggest possible routes for later testing by the project team; this interpretation links measurable pilot evidence with credibility, learning, and continued support for innovation.

The pilot's verified reduction in delivery time while meeting all required safety standards; this interpretation links measurable pilot evidence with credibility, learning, and continued support for innovation.
questions.x: The verified, measurable pilot result (3 h → 40 min, safely) = a short-term win.
